intent: Build an HTTP service that turns long URLs into short codes, redirects short codes to their targets, persists links durably, and reports click analytics per link.
assumptions: 'Scalable' means a stateless app tier that scales horizontally over one Postgres, not a multi-region design.
Analytics means per-link click counts over time and top referrers; no user accounts or dashboards.
Links are anonymous; there is no authentication or per-user ownership.
Optional custom aliases and optional expiry are in scope because they change the data model and are cheap now.
acceptance_criteria: POST /links returns a short code for any valid http(s) URL and rejects other schemes.
GET /{code} redirects to the target URL; unknown codes return 404 and expired links 410.
Codes are unique, non-sequential and collision-safe under concurrent creation.
Every redirect is recorded as a click with timestamp and referrer.
GET /links/{code}/stats returns total clicks, clicks per day and top referrers.
Links and clicks persist in Postgres; unit and integration tests pass.
